1283.title: Trolley Problem in AI
1283.heading: Trolley Problem in AI
1283.content:
The trolley problem in AI applies a forced-choice moral dilemma to an autonomous system, often asking how a self-driving vehicle should distribute unavoidable harm. It is useful for revealing conflicts among principles and for asking who is authorized to encode a choice.

Its artificial simplicity can misrepresent real engineering. Actual safety decisions involve uncertain perception, probabilities, design trade-offs, maintenance, law, and opportunities to prevent the dangerous situation before a final collision choice exists. Ethical design should therefore not reduce [[Functional Morality]] to selecting a victim in a stylized scenario.

1286.heading: Trojan Horse Malware
1286.content:
Trojan horse malware presents itself as legitimate or desirable software while concealing a harmful function. Its success depends on persuading a user or administrator to install or run it, rather than on self-replication.

The deceptive packaging connects this [[Host-Based Malware]] to [[Social Engineering]]. Software provenance, restricted privileges, application controls, and user caution reduce the opportunity for a disguised program to establish access or deliver another payload.

1289.title: Trivial Ring
1289.heading: Trivial Ring
1289.content:
The trivial ring has one element, so its additive and multiplicative identities coincide. It satisfies the ring axioms but is excluded from definitions that require a nonzero ring.

Its characteristic is one, a case separated from the zero or prime characteristics of nontrivial finite domains.

1292.title: Trivial Solution
1292.heading: Trivial Solution
1292.content:
The trivial solution of a [[Homogeneous Linear System]] is the zero vector. It always satisfies $Ax=0$ because multiplying any matrix by the zero vector gives zero.

A nonsingular square system has only this homogeneous solution. Nontrivial solutions exist when the coefficient matrix has a nonzero null space.

1294.sourceSearchName: tritium breeding blanket tritium breeding blanket

1295.sourceSearchName: tritium breeding blanket tritium breeding blanket
1295.title: Tritium Breeding Blanket
1295.heading: Tritium Breeding Blanket
1295.content: A breeding blanket surrounds fusion plasma with lithium-containing material. Neutrons from the [[Deuterium-Tritium Fusion Reaction]] interact with lithium to make replacement [[Tritium]] and release heat. The source places this blanket outside the plasma wall in its tokamak arrangement, with subsequent tritium recovery. It addresses limited natural tritium supply while also linking fuel production to reactor heat extraction.

1298.title: Tritium
1298.heading: Tritium
1298.content: Tritium is a hydrogen isotope whose nucleus contains one proton and two neutrons. It is a reactant in the [[Deuterium-Tritium Fusion Reaction]], but the source notes that it is not abundant as a natural fuel supply. A reactor can make more by exposing lithium in a [[Tritium Breeding Blanket]] to fusion neutrons, so fuel recovery becomes part of the plant design.

1301.title: Trinomial
1301.heading: Trinomial
1301.content:
A trinomial is a [[Polynomial]] with three terms. A common one-variable form is

$$ax^2+bx+c,$$

called a quadratic trinomial when (a\neq0). A trinomial may be the expansion of two [[Binomial]] factors, but not every trinomial factors over integers.

Recognizing coefficients and signs supports [[Quadratic Trinomial Factorization]]. A perfect square trinomial has the special structure (a^2\pm2ab+b^2), while a general quadratic may require completing the square or the quadratic formula.

1304.title: Trigonometric Ratios
1304.heading: Trigonometric Ratios
1304.content: For an acute angle in a right triangle, sine is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, and tangent is opposite over adjacent. Their reciprocal ratios are cosecant, secant, and cotangent. Similarity makes these ratios depend on the angle rather than the triangle's size, allowing angle and side measurements to determine one another.

1306.sourceSearchName: triangular potential element triangular potential element
1306.title: Triangular Potential Element
1306.heading: Document

1307.sourceSearchName: triangular potential element triangular potential element
1307.title: Triangular Potential Element
1307.heading: Triangular Potential Element
1307.content:
A triangular potential element uses three nodal values to define a linear scalar potential over a two-dimensional triangle. Counterclockwise node ordering and vertex coordinates determine the shape functions and element area.

Because the potential varies linearly, its gradient and the associated field are constant within the element. A mesh of triangles approximates spatially changing fields through piecewise-constant gradients.

1308.sourceSearchName: triangular potential element triangular potential element
1308.title: Triangular Potential Element
1308.heading: References

1310.title: Trigonometric Periodicity
1310.heading: Trigonometric Periodicity
1310.content: A periodic function repeats its values after a fixed positive interval. Sine and cosine have period $2\pi$, while tangent has period $\pi$. These periods follow from repeated positions or slopes on the [[Unit Circle]] and allow infinitely many angles to share the same trigonometric value.

1313.title: Tridiagonal Matrix
1313.heading: Tridiagonal Matrix
1313.content:
A tridiagonal matrix is a banded square matrix whose nonzero entries lie only on the main diagonal, superdiagonal, and subdiagonal.

Its restricted structure makes [[Gaussian Elimination]] and [[LU Decomposition]] much cheaper than for a dense matrix. Such systems occur in discretized differential-equation and heat-conduction models.

1316.title: Triclustering
1316.heading: Triclustering
1316.content:
Triclustering extends biclustering to a third dimension such as time, patient, or experimental replicate. A result identifies a coherent subarray rather than a single global partition of each axis.

The extension can reveal context-specific temporal expression, but the search space grows rapidly and overlapping patterns become common. Statistical significance and redundancy controls are needed to distinguish useful structures from flexible fits.

1318.sourceSearchName: triangular membership function triangular membership function
1318.title: Triangular Membership Function
1318.heading: Document

1319.sourceSearchName: triangular membership function triangular membership function
1319.title: Triangular Membership Function
1319.heading: Triangular Membership Function
1319.content:
A triangular membership function rises linearly from zero to a peak membership of one and then falls linearly to zero. Three parameters identify its left boundary, peak, and right boundary.

Its simple shape is easy to implement and interpret for ordered linguistic categories. Adjacent triangles can overlap to express gradual transitions among labels.

1322.content:
Triangular and curved fin side profiles vary thickness or edge position along the fin length instead of using a constant rectangular outline. Concave, convex, triangular, and trapezoidal-concave profiles can be defined with parameterized points and curves.

The profile controls both volume and exposed area, so comparisons should normalize the quantity relevant to the design. Smooth appearance alone does not establish better thermal performance or easier meshing.

1325.title: Triangle Congruence
1325.heading: Triangle Congruence
1325.content: Two triangles are congruent when they are equal in size and shape, so corresponding sides and angles agree. Standard sufficient criteria include side-side-side, side-angle-side, and angle-side-angle; right triangles also admit hypotenuse-leg reasoning. Congruence turns a limited set of measurements into conclusions about every corresponding part.

1328.heading: Triangle Angle Sum
1328.content: The interior angles of a Euclidean triangle sum to $180^\circ$. Drawing a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side transfers the other two angles by alternate-angle relationships; the three then form a straight angle. The result depends on Euclidean parallel geometry and does not hold unchanged for a [[Spherical Triangle]].

In a game environment, one hue usually carries most of the scene while the other two serve secondary structures and accents. Adjusting saturation and value prevents the palette from reading as three equally loud signals.

1337.content:
Tree-structured feature selection incorporates hierarchical relations among variables. A feature may represent a broad category whose descendants encode progressively narrower alternatives, so a valid subset should respect ancestry or descendant constraints.

Using the hierarchy can stabilize selection and keep the result interpretable at an appropriate level of detail. The selection rule must specify whether choosing a child requires its ancestors or whether choosing a parent substitutes for its descendants.

1340.content:
Tree-based itemset mining compresses transactions or candidate prefixes into a shared branching structure. Common prefixes reuse nodes, and traversal extends only branches that can still satisfy support and constraint requirements.

In distributed uncertain mining, local trees find candidate patterns before global evidence is combined, reducing unnecessary transmission of raw transactions.

1343.title: Tree Shaking
1343.heading: Tree Shaking
1343.content:
Tree shaking is a build optimization that removes unused code from the final JavaScript bundle. Smaller bundles reduce code transferred to and processed by the browser.

Angular services provided through root-level injectable metadata can participate in this optimization because the build system can determine whether the service is used. Registering code in ways that create unavoidable references can prevent removal.

The .NET Core 3 desktop discussion applies the same removal idea to application publication: unused runtime components can be excluded while producing a compact deployment, including a single executable. The result depends on the publisher being able to determine which code is reachable.

1346.title: Tree Pruning
1346.heading: Tree Pruning
1346.content:
Tree pruning removes branches or subtrees that add complexity without improving reliable classification. It aims to discard patterns caused by noise or sampling accidents.

Pruning can occur during growth or after a larger tree is built. A separate validation set, a statistical test, or a minimum-description criterion can guide the decision.

1349.sourceSearchName: tree branch permutation symmetry tree branch permutation symmetry
1349.title: Tree Branch Permutation Symmetry
1349.heading: Tree Branch Permutation Symmetry
1349.content:
Swapping the two child branches below a dendrogram node changes the page order of leaves but not the membership of clusters inside either subtree. Such adjacency-preserving permutations are tree symmetries; the book describes their combined actions through a wreath-product group.

This distinguishes a hierarchy's intrinsic nested structure from an arbitrary left-right drawing convention. A summary constant within a cluster is invariant under these branch exchanges, providing a mathematical basis for multiscale aggregation on a tree.

1352.title: Tree Ancestor Distance
1352.heading: Tree Ancestor Distance
1352.content:
In a ranked dendrogram, the distance between two leaves can be read from the level at which their branches first share a common ancestor. Nearby leaves join low in the hierarchy; leaves from distant branches meet at a higher level.

This cophenetic or ancestor distance is ultrametric when merge levels rise consistently toward the root. It turns the tree into a distance representation, so the same hierarchy can support cluster cuts, proximity queries, and analysis of how data structure changes with resolution.

A treatment contrast expresses a comparison among fitted group means as a linear combination of model coefficients. It turns the parameterization of a [[Design Matrix]] into the scientific difference an investigator wants to estimate or test.

Changing a [[Regression Reference Group]] changes the displayed coefficients but not a properly specified contrast among the same group means. Explicit contrasts are especially useful when factors and interactions make the desired comparison span several terms.

1361.title: Traveling Wave Equation
1361.heading: Traveling Wave Equation
1361.content:
A sinusoidal wave traveling in the positive $x$ direction can be written

$$y(x,t)=A\cos(\omega t-kx+\phi_0).$$

Here $A$ is amplitude, $\omega=2\pi f$, and $k=2\pi/\lambda$. A surface of constant phase moves at $v=\omega/k=f\lambda$. Reversing the sign before $kx$ reverses the propagation direction under this convention.

1364.title: Traveling Salesman Problem
1364.heading: Traveling Salesman Problem
1364.content:
The traveling salesman problem asks for the shortest tour that visits every city in a given collection once and returns to the starting city, using known distances between each pair.

Enumerating every ordering of $n$ cities produces [[Factorial Time Complexity]], so brute force becomes unusable quickly. The problem is a standard example of an [[Intractable Problem]] for which practical work often relies on an [[Approximation Algorithm]] that finds a good route without guaranteeing the absolute shortest one.

1367.title: Transverse Wave
1367.heading: Transverse Wave
1367.content: A transverse wave has oscillations perpendicular to its direction of energy transfer. The displacement can occur in any direction within the plane normal to propagation, which makes [[Polarization]] possible. Electromagnetic waves and waves on a stretched string are transverse, although their physical disturbances are different.

1370.content: The transverse Mercator rotates the ordinary Mercator cylinder so its tangency follows a meridian rather than the Equator. Scale is true along that central meridian and remains acceptable within a limited band on either side. This makes the projection well suited to regions whose north-south extent is much greater than their east-west width.

1373.title: Transposition Method
1373.heading: Transposition Method
1373.content:
The transposition method is a [[Self-Organizing Search]] strategy that swaps a found item with the item immediately before it. Each successful access moves the target forward by one position unless it is already first.

Popular items accumulate repeated forward moves and eventually gather near the head, while seldom-used items drift backward. It adapts more slowly than the [[Move-to-Front Algorithm]] but can produce a stronger long-term ordering by access frequency.

1376.title: Transport Layer
1376.heading: Transport Layer
1376.content:
The transport layer delivers data between endpoint processes and determines what reliability, ordering, flow management, segmentation, and connection behavior the transport protocol supplies. TCP and UDP represent different choices within this responsibility.

Transport does not decide the business meaning of an HTTP request or the route between networks. It supplies the delivery service on which those higher-level interactions depend.

1385.title: Transmission Control Protocol
1385.heading: Transmission Control Protocol
1385.content:
Transmission Control Protocol provides a reliable ordered data stream over an unreliable packet network. It divides application data, tracks delivery, retransmits missing pieces, and reassembles the original sequence.

TCP operates end to end between hosts rather than requiring every network link to guarantee delivery. Applications can use its service without managing each packet directly.

This reliability can add delay when a missing segment blocks later data until retransmission succeeds. Games therefore use TCP for information that must arrive intact, while rapidly changing real-time updates often favor [[User Datagram Protocol]].

1388.title: Translating Words into Algebra
1388.heading: Translating Words into Algebra
1388.content:
Translating words into algebra represents a verbal relationship with variables and operation symbols. Terms such as sum, difference, product, quotient, square, and reciprocal indicate operations, while phrasing determines their order.

Order matters for noncommutative operations. "A number decreased by seven" is (x-7), whereas "seven decreased by a number" is (7-x). Grouping also matters: tripling a number and then adding five gives (3x+5), while tripling the result after adding five gives (3(x+5)). A correct translation models the relationship, not merely the vocabulary.

1391.title: Transitive Property of Inequality
1391.heading: Transitive Property of Inequality
1391.content:
The transitive property of inequality states that an ordering can pass through an intermediate value. If

$$a<b\quad\text{and}\quad b<c,$$

then

$$a<c.$$

The property allows separate comparisons to be chained and justifies the order represented on a [[Number Line]]. It also supports compound bounds: if a variable is greater than a lower boundary and less than an upper boundary, its solution belongs between them, subject to whether each endpoint is strict or inclusive.

1394.title: Transitive Game Balance
1394.heading: Transitive Game Balance
1394.content:
In the source's terminology, transitive game balance is a circular relationship in which each type defeats some peers and is defeated by others, as in rock-paper-scissors. No one part dominates the whole system.

The structure uses an odd number of peer types so each can have a clear advantage over half and disadvantage against half of the others. External factors must still perturb the ecology enough to preserve strategy without producing a dominant path.

1397.title: Transitive Closure
1397.heading: Transitive Closure
1397.content:
The transitive closure R* of a [[Binary Relation]] R relates a to b when a finite sequence of one or more R-steps leads from a to b. It is the smallest transitive relation containing the original relation.

If R records direct flights between cities, R* records every destination reachable through a sequence of flights. The construction converts local adjacency into multi-step reachability.

1400.title: Transitional Interface
1400.heading: Transitional Interface
1400.content:
A transitional interface animates the change between two related viewpoints or representations instead of replacing one abruptly. In navigation, it can connect an egocentric AR view to an exocentric overview while showing how position, scale, and orientation transform.

The visible transition preserves context and reduces the mental effort required to match objects across views. Its duration and path should explain the relationship without delaying the user's task unnecessarily.

1403.title: Transit Navigation Satellite System
1403.heading: Transit Navigation Satellite System
1403.content: Transit was a US Navy satellite-navigation system developed to update the inertial positions of ballistic-missile submarines. Its polar-orbiting satellites broadcast stable frequencies and orbital data; a receiver inferred location from the Doppler curve during a pass. Transit supplied latitude and longitude rather than continuous three-dimensional navigation, yet its long operational life proved that a passive space-based service could support both military and unanticipated civilian users.

1406.title: Transistor Invention at Bell Labs
1406.heading: Transistor Invention at Bell Labs
1406.content:
William Shockley, Walter Brattain, and John Bardeen developed the first successful transistor at Bell Laboratories in 1947. The solid-state device could switch or amplify current without a vacuum or heated filament.

Bell Labs disclosed and licensed the invention rather than keeping it classified. Years of further materials and manufacturing work were required before transistors transformed computers.

Time-step size and integration method must resolve both the load variation and important structural modes. Initial conditions and damping influence the computed response.

1415.title: Transhumanism
1415.heading: Transhumanism
1415.content:
Transhumanism supports using science and technology to overcome limits of the human condition, including limits on cognition, health, lifespan, and bodily capability. AI appears in transhumanist visions as an enhancement, a partner with which humans might merge, or a route toward intelligence and life no longer constrained by the biological body.

The vision raises questions about access, inequality, and what counts as improvement. It can also express a desire to escape embodiment and earthly dependence. [[Posthumanism]] challenges human centrality from another direction: instead of perfecting humanity, it questions why human traits should define intelligence and value in the first place.

1418.title: Transformer
1418.heading: Transformer
1418.content: A transformer transfers alternating electrical energy between coils through changing magnetic flux in a shared core. For an ideal transformer, $V_s/V_p=N_s/N_p$ and input power equals output power, so increasing voltage decreases current. High-voltage transmission reduces resistive losses for a given delivered power.

1424.content:

1427.title: Transcendental Element
1427.heading: Transcendental Element
1427.content:
An element of an extension is transcendental over K when no nonzero polynomial in K[x] has it as a root. It therefore satisfies no algebraic relation with coefficients in K.

The book contrasts familiar algebraic radicals with transcendental real numbers such as e and π over the rationals.

1430.title: Transactional Scheduler
1430.heading: Transactional Scheduler
1430.content:
A transactional scheduler orders or delays transactions to reduce conflicts before the concurrency-control mechanism forces aborts. Reactive scheduling learns from observed collisions, while dependency-aware scheduling can use known relationships between abstract operations and data objects.

The scheduler trades some immediate parallelism for less wasted work and higher committed throughput.

1432.sourceSearchName: transaction based pricing transaction based pricing
1432.title: Transaction-Based Pricing
1432.heading: Document

1433.sourceSearchName: transaction based pricing transaction based pricing
1433.title: Transaction-Based Pricing
1433.heading: Transaction-Based Pricing
1433.content:
Transaction-based pricing charges for discrete units of work such as invoices processed, information requests, application operations, or another countable business event. A unit price can be estimated by dividing the service's cost by its expected transaction volume.

The model works best when transactions are clearly defined, their volumes are predictable, and the volume follows the provider's cost drivers. It is particularly suitable for information and business-process services.

1434.title: Transaction-Based Pricing
1434.heading: References

1436.title: Transacted Message
1436.heading: Transacted Message
1436.content:
A transacted message participates in an end-to-end transaction or business function. Delivery is considered complete only when the associated transaction commits rather than merely when the message arrives at a receiver.

This connects messaging success to a wider unit of work. The transaction boundary, rollback behavior, and participating systems must be defined so a transport acknowledgment is not mistaken for completed business processing.

1439.title: Transaction Boundary
1439.heading: Transaction Boundary
1439.content: A transaction boundary identifies the state changes that must succeed or fail together. In a domain-centered model, an [[Aggregate]] defines this boundary rather than allowing each controller or database routine to choose an arbitrary group of records. A command begins with a valid aggregate and must finish with either a valid new state or the original state. Keeping the boundary small reduces unrelated write conflicts and prevents one business operation from locking an excessive object graph.

1442.title: Transaction Database
1442.heading: Transaction Database
1442.content:
A transaction database is a finite collection of records, each containing a set of items that occurred together. A shopping basket is the standard example, but a transaction can represent any co-occurring categorical events.

Association-rule methods scan the database to count itemsets and discover combinations that meet support and confidence requirements.

1445.title: Trajectory Clustering
1445.heading: Trajectory Clustering
1445.content:
Trajectory clustering groups moving objects from sequences of spatial positions, possibly augmented with time, speed, direction, or context. Similarity may compare complete paths, aligned subtrajectories, stops, or common route segments.

Different applications care about different invariances: two travelers may share a route at different times, or occupy the same places in a different order. The representation should make the intended notion of shared movement explicit.

1448.content:
Training performance bias is the optimistic error estimate produced by evaluating a model on the observations used to fit it. Flexible learners can adapt to sample-specific noise and appear nearly perfect without generalizing.

A [[Validation Dataset]] or [[Test Dataset]] is required to estimate out-of-sample behavior.

1451.title: Training Dataset
1451.heading: Training Dataset
1451.content:
A training dataset is the collection of examples from which a machine-learning model estimates its parameters. Its coverage, labels, and errors shape the behavior the model can learn.

For speech systems, useful training data must span speakers, accents, recording conditions, and acoustic environments while pairing audio with accurate transcriptions. A large dataset that omits important variation can still produce a brittle [[Acoustic Model]].

Training data are also a [[Dataset Abstraction]] shaped by choices about categories, labels, and inclusion. Their size does not guarantee [[Dataset Representativeness]], and records of earlier decisions can encode [[Historical Bias in Data]]. A model may therefore reproduce social inequality while accurately learning the pattern it was given.

During supervised neural-network training, each example is paired with a desired output. One complete pass through the collection is a [[Training Epoch]], and multiple epochs progressively adjust weights and biases. A separate [[Test Dataset]] is withheld from these updates so it can measure generalization.

For the source's tissue-classification problem, the training dataset contains gene-expression features paired with known tissue labels. It supports fitting and parameter selection, but performance measured on the same observations is an optimistically biased estimate of prediction on new samples.

Kelleher describes a dataset as examples represented by features, with target values added for supervised learning. Choosing too few features can hide useful information, while irrelevant or redundant features can invite spurious patterns. Large neural datasets help flexible models learn, yet scale alone cannot settle the [[Ill-Posed Learning Problem|ambiguity]] between several functions or remove the need to check generalization.

The book's predictive pattern assigns most records to training while preserving separate validation and test partitions. Training is the only partition used to fit model parameters; its apparent performance is expected to be optimistic.

1454.title: Training Epoch
1454.heading: Training Epoch
1454.content:
A training epoch is one complete pass through every example in a [[Training Dataset]]. During the pass, the learning procedure produces outputs, measures loss, and updates the model's parameters.

Training commonly uses multiple epochs so later passes begin from parameters improved during earlier ones. Too many passes can make the model conform too closely to the training examples, producing [[Overfitting]] and weaker results on a [[Test Dataset]].

1457.title: Training Error
1457.heading: Training Error
1457.content:
Training error measures prediction mistakes on the same observations used to fit a model. It describes how closely the learned rule conforms to its [[Training Dataset]] but usually understates error on new data.

A more flexible method can lower training error even after generalization begins to worsen. The source's one-neighbor classifier reaches zero training error by matching every point to itself, providing an extreme example of why training fit cannot select a model alone.

In the book's examples, very strong or perfect training results are treated as a warning rather than proof of success. Validation error reveals whether added complexity is learning transferable structure or merely reproducing the training partition.

1459.sourceSearchName: training and test datasets training and test datasets
1459.title: Training and Test Datasets
1459.heading: Document

1460.sourceSearchName: training and test datasets training and test datasets
1460.title: Training and Test Datasets
1460.heading: Training and Test Datasets
1460.content:
Training data is used to fit a model's parameters, while test data is withheld to estimate how the learned model behaves on unseen examples. Evaluating on the same observations used for fitting gives an overly optimistic picture of generalization.

The split must preserve the structure of the real prediction problem and avoid leaking future or duplicate information across partitions. Representative test data makes metrics meaningful; a mechanically random split does not correct a biased or inappropriate dataset.

1463.title: Trained Rather Than Programmed Systems
1463.heading: Trained Rather Than Programmed Systems
1463.content:
A trained system acquires internal parameters from examples or interaction rather than having every decision rule written by a programmer. The training algorithm defines how parameters change, while data and objectives shape the resulting behavior.

This shifts computational design toward dataset construction, evaluation, and control of generalization. The absence of hand-written rules does not remove human responsibility for the model, training process, or deployment context.

1466.content:
The tragedy of the commons is a system pattern in which individuals acting in their own short-term interest deplete a limited shared resource. Each actor receives a concentrated benefit while the cost is distributed across the group.

The pattern can create conflict and strategic play when the shared [[Resource]] and its depletion are legible. Without meaningful coordination or balancing mechanisms, the common stock can collapse even though no participant intended that collective outcome.

1469.title: Tracking Update Rate
1469.heading: Tracking Update Rate
1469.content:
Tracking update rate is the number of sensor measurements produced in a unit of time. A higher rate provides more frequent pose information and can describe fast motion more closely, provided the readings are useful and reach the application promptly.

Update rate is distinct from latency. A tracker may report many measurements per second while each measurement arrives too late for correct visual registration, so both temporal properties must be evaluated.

1472.title: Tracking Precision
1472.heading: Tracking Precision
1472.content:
Tracking precision describes how closely repeated measurements of the same physical quantity agree with one another. It varies by sensor type and may differ among the position and orientation degrees of freedom.

Random measurement error limits precision. Filtering can make readings more consistent, but may increase computational cost and latency; a steadier augmentation is not useful if it lags noticeably behind motion.

1475.title: Tracking Pattern Search and Anchor Regions
1475.heading: Tracking Pattern Search and Anchor Regions
1475.content: A two-dimensional tracker separates three jobs: a pattern region describes the image feature to recognize, a search region bounds where to look for it in the next frame, and an anchor locates the point whose motion will be applied. A good pattern has enough stable, distinct texture to be found repeatedly. An anchor can be placed at the desired attachment point even when the recognizable feature is nearby rather than exactly on that point. Search size must be tuned, as described in [[Tracker Search Window Tuning]].

1478.title: Tracking Jitter
1478.heading: Tracking Jitter
1478.content:
Tracking jitter is rapid random variation in reported pose even when the tracked object is still or moving smoothly. In an augmented display, that noise makes virtual content appear to shake relative to its physical reference.

Temporal filtering can suppress high-frequency variation, but it introduces delay and can attenuate real motion. Filter strength must therefore be chosen with both visual stability and registration latency in mind.

1481.title: Tracking Accuracy
1481.heading: Tracking Accuracy
1481.content:
Tracking accuracy describes how close a measured pose or quantity is to its true value. It is primarily limited by systematic errors in the sensor, its model, installation, or calibration.

High precision does not guarantee high accuracy: repeated readings may agree closely while all remain biased. Better calibration can reduce that bias, but the effort and cost must be justified by the registration demands of the application.

1484.sourceSearchName: tracker search window tuning tracker search window tuning
1484.title: Tracker Search Window Tuning
1484.heading: Tracker Search Window Tuning
1484.content: The search region must be large enough to contain the feature's next-frame motion but not so large that a similar feature elsewhere becomes a tempting match. A tiny pattern may lock onto grain rather than a durable image detail, while an oversized pattern includes changing material that weakens recognition. When a track fails, inspect both the selected feature and its search boundary before assuming the entire shot is untrackable. The pattern, search, and anchor roles are separated in [[Tracking Pattern Search and Anchor Regions]].
links: Tracking Pattern Search and Anchor Regions

1487.title: Tracker Drift
1487.heading: Tracker Drift
1487.content:
Tracker drift is accumulated pose error that grows as relative measurements are integrated over time. Gyroscopes, accelerometers, odometers, and incremental visual trackers can follow short-term change well while their estimate gradually departs from the physical reference.

An absolute measurement or recognized location can correct the accumulated error. Sensor fusion and visual loop closure use such evidence to retain responsive local tracking without allowing the reference frame to wander indefinitely.

1490.title: Tracer Bullet
1490.heading: Tracer Bullet
1490.content:
A tracer bullet is a thin, representative path through a larger body of work. By implementing one realistic slice across relevant layers, a team learns about integration, performance, workflow, and cost before estimating or committing to the full set.

Unlike a disposable research [[Spike]], a tracer bullet is working product evidence. Its purpose is not breadth or polish but reducing uncertainty with an end-to-end example.

1493.content:

Trace levels filter events by severity or importance. A runtime configuration can suppress routine information while preserving warnings and errors, making production diagnostics less noisy. Listeners should be flushed and closed so buffered records reach their destination.

1499.heading: TOTEM
1499.content:
TOTEM is a heterogeneous graph-processing system that partitions graph work between CPUs and GPUs. It aims to use GPU throughput while retaining CPU memory capacity and flexible control for work less suited to the accelerator.

Partition choice and communication across the host-device boundary determine whether heterogeneous execution outperforms either processor alone.

A torsion-free module has no nonzero element annihilated by a non-zero-divisor of the ring. Over an [[Integral Domain]], rm = 0 with r and m nonzero cannot occur.

For a module over a Noetherian integral domain, torsion-freeness corresponds to the zero ideal being its only [[Associated Prime]]. It is weaker than freeness but preserves cancellation by nonzero scalars.

Over a Noetherian integral domain, M is torsion exactly when the zero ideal is not an [[Associated Prime]]. Torsion records elements supported away from the generic prime.

Its magnitude is $\tau=F d_\perp$, where $d_\perp$ is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force's line of action; equivalently, $\tau=rF\sin\theta$. Torque is a vector and changes angular momentum just as force changes linear momentum.

1520.title: Tor Functor
1520.heading: Tor Functor

Tor is symmetric in M and N over a commutative ring. Positive-degree Tor measures the failure of tensor product to preserve exactness and vanishes for [[Flat Module]]s.

1529.title: Top-of-Descent Rule of Three
1529.heading: Top-of-Descent Rule of Three
1529.content: For a path near three degrees, multiply the desired altitude loss in thousands of feet by three to estimate descent distance in nautical miles. Losing 7,000 feet therefore calls for a top of descent about 21 nautical miles before the target. The approximation is slightly shallower than the exact tangent relationship and should be refined when procedure constraints demand it.

1532.title: Token-Based Authentication
1532.heading: Token-Based Authentication
1532.content:
Token-based authentication gives a client a token after successful authentication and requires that token on later protected requests. The server validates the token rather than retrieving all authentication state from a dedicated session.

The ASP.NET Core and Angular SPA flow uses a [[JSON Web Token]] issued through IdentityServer. An [[HTTP Interceptor]] can attach the token to outgoing client requests.

1535.title: Tokamak Fusion Reactor
1535.heading: Tokamak Fusion Reactor
1535.content: A tokamak is a toroidal reactor arrangement for [[Magnetic Fusion Confinement]]. Magnets guide the charged plasma inside an evacuated chamber, while escaping fusion neutrons transfer energy to surrounding structures and a lithium blanket can breed fuel. The source's diagram also shows heat removal, helium handling, and tritium separation. The magnetic chamber is only one part of a potential electricity-generating plant.
